decision.rationale: Required CI is green, but three high-confidence critical defects break the credential authorization boundary, OpenAPI compatibility gate, and exact release/Skill binding of the confirmed core journey. AGILE_REVIEWED permits blocking only for critical findings, and all three meet that threshold.

findings.title: Failed credential revalidation preserves stale VERIFIED authority
findings.observation: For an identity-identical profile, storeProfile supports UNVERIFIED-to-VERIFIED but otherwise returns the existing file. A current UNVERIFIED candidate from a real 401/403 therefore cannot invalidate an existing VERIFIED result, and initializeProfile derives credentialVerified from the stale returned profile.
findings.trigger: Initialize a profile successfully, then revoke or invalidate the same bearer and rerun isolated synthetic verification with unchanged identity fields.
findings.impact: The CLI can claim PROFILE_VERIFIED for a credential that the authoritative API has just rejected, breaking the authentication boundary and credential revalidation requirements.

evidence.description: An existing VERIFIED profile followed by an identity-identical UNVERIFIED candidate returned the old VERIFIED profile with changed=false.
initializeProfile reports stored.profile.validation.credentialUsability, so the stale state becomes the command result.

findings.remediation: Make a current failed or unknown credential check fail closed and prevent old positive evidence from being reported as current. Define whether the file is downgraded, replaced, or preserved with an explicit failing result that cannot authorize a write.
findings.verification: Add an integration regression that verifies a profile, causes the same token to return 401/403, reruns initialization, and asserts no VERIFIED result or success claim survives.

findings.title: Incompatible request and response schemas produce the same OpenAPI digest
findings.observation: The projection retains only route/method presence, response status names, bearer-security presence and request-body requiredness. It omits every consumed schema, field, parameter and component definition.
findings.trigger: Deploy an API that keeps the same paths/statuses/security but removes proposer/actor fields or replaces a required request/response schema.
findings.impact: Initialization records openapi=VERIFIED and permits handoff to a business Skill whose core requests can no longer be formed or read correctly.

evidence.description: Replacing Idea POST with a required string body and deleting all component schemas produced the same compatibility digest as the canonical LP-03 document.
Acceptance criteria require OpenAPI contract compatibility and stable clientId/displayName attribution fields before continuing to the business Skill.

findings.remediation: Hash the exact required contract or expand and normalize the compatibility projection to every request, response, parameter, actor and security shape consumed by both Skills.
findings.verification: Add negative fixtures for removed/renamed actor fields, changed request bodies, response envelopes, path parameters and referenced schemas; each must return OPENAPI_INCOMPATIBLE.

findings.title: Release and Skill claims are not bound to the local Skill bytes
findings.observation: The profile combines a caller-supplied handoff commit/version with a digest of a separately caller-selected Skill root without proving their relationship. No runtime call verifies the local tree against the declared commit/version or the endpoint against the declared release/source commit.
findings.trigger: Supply any syntactically valid or nonexistent Skill commit together with a different local Skill tree and an otherwise compatible loopback API.
findings.impact: The initializer can emit a fully VERIFIED profile whose advertised exact release/Skill authority does not identify the instructions actually loaded, defeating mismatch detection for the core client journey.

evidence.description: The passing HTTP integration uses skillCommit equal to forty b characters, computes the current repository Skill tree, and asserts credentialVerified=true.
Repository search found no call to assertProfileMatchesHandoff and no Git/object or expected-tree verification in the initializer.

findings.remediation: Define a closed handoff authority that carries or derives the expected Skill tree/version and deployed release identity, then verify those claims against the local bytes and observed target before writing a usable profile.
findings.verification: Add fail-closed tests for nonexistent/wrong Skill commit, wrong tree, wrong version, release/source mismatch and caller-selected alternate Skill roots, plus a positive exact-binding case.

required_actions.action: Prevent current credential failure from preserving or reporting stale VERIFIED usability.
Make OpenAPI verification cover the full contract surface consumed by the Skills.
Cryptographically or deterministically bind release/Skill claims to the actual local Skill bytes and target authority.

risks.description: Stale authorization evidence can be reported as current after the API rejects the bearer.
risks.mitigation: Resolve PRR-001 and retain a revocation/revalidation regression.

risks.description: The compatibility digest admits API shapes that cannot complete the core workflow.
risks.mitigation: Resolve PRR-002 with schema-sensitive compatibility tests.

risks.description: Profile release and Skill identifiers need not correspond to the deployed or locally loaded bytes.
risks.mitigation: Resolve PRR-003 with explicit authority binding and mismatch tests.
